name: ShepherdCare
shortDescription: A UK-developed pastoral-care and church-administration platform for care requests, visits, prayer, events, teams and member communication.
suitableContexts: Churches seeking a focused pastoral-care request and follow-up workflow
Teams that want pastoral visits, prayer, events and member coordination in one newer product

pricing.summary: The supplier advertises a free tier for up to 15 members. Ask the supplier for current paid-plan prices.

tiers.label: Free tier
tiers.detail: Supplier advertises use for up to 15 members

gdprInformation: The supplier describes the application as multi-tenant and secure. Ask for its privacy terms, data-processing agreement, hosting location, retention and export arrangements.
coreFeatures: Home, hospital, prayer and counselling-visit tracking

uk-purchasing.value: Nathanoak describes itself as UK-based and identifies ShepherdCare as a live production pastoral-care product.

volunteer-usability.value: Supplier describes ministry teams and a Sunday service roster.

editorial.assessment: ShepherdCare addresses a useful but sensitive operational gap: coordinating requests, visits and follow-up without relying solely on memory or informal messages. It is a newer product with significant due-diligence gaps, so a church should begin with a low-risk trial and agree what information should never be stored before putting pastoral history into the system.
bestFor: Small church pastoral teams wanting a structured request and visit workflow
Churches that need basic member, event and rota features alongside pastoral coordination
Teams prepared to start with a limited, carefully governed pilot
strengths: Pastoral requests, visits, prayer and follow-up are explicit product functions
A free tier is advertised for up to 15 members
Supplier presents it as a live UK-developed product
limitations: Ask the supplier about Paid pricing, company registration, privacy terms, hosting, processor terms, retention and exports
Pastoral notes may be highly sensitive; the church must set firm access and recording boundaries
The product cannot replace safeguarding response, emergency services, professional care or pastoral judgement

procurementVerdict.problem: Church pastoral teams needing a structured request and follow-up workflow
procurementVerdict.differentiator: Care requests, visit tracking and prayer coordination are core rather than incidental functions
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Run a limited pilot with agreed data boundaries and test access, handover, safeguarding escalation and exit arrangements
